quests.instruction: Your best friend starts spending more time with a new kid at school. How do you feel?
quests.question: Jealous
quests.hint: Watching a friend share their time with someone new can give you an uncomfortable, wanting feeling.
quests.explanation: Watching a close friend spend time with someone new can give you an uncomfortable, wanting feeling.
quests.funFact: Friend groups can grow bigger without anyone getting less friendship — there is room for everyone!

quests.instruction: You do not get picked for the part you really wanted in the play. How do you feel?
quests.question: Disappointed
quests.hint: Trying your best for a role and not getting it can leave you with a heavy feeling.
quests.explanation: Trying your best for something and not getting it can leave you with a heavy, letdown feeling.
quests.funFact: Every part in a play, even a small one, helps make the whole show come together!

quests.instruction: You trip over your own shoelace during a school assembly. How do you feel?
quests.question: Embarrassed
quests.hint: A small stumble in front of a big group can make your cheeks feel warm.
quests.explanation: A small stumble in front of a big group can make your cheeks feel warm and shy for a moment.
quests.funFact: Double-knotting your shoelaces in the morning can help this happen a little less often!

quests.instruction: Your neighbor helps you carry your heavy bags up the stairs. How do you feel?
quests.question: Thankful
quests.hint: Having someone offer help when you needed it can make your heart feel warm.
quests.explanation: Having someone offer help right when you needed it fills your heart with a warm, grateful feeling.
quests.funFact: Saying 'thank you' out loud helps both you and the helper feel good!

quests.instruction: You are about to ride the biggest roller coaster at the fair for the first time. How do you feel?
quests.question: Nervous
quests.hint: Waiting in line for something big and new can make your tummy flutter.
quests.explanation: Waiting for something big and new can give your tummy a fluttery, excited-but-unsure feeling.
quests.funFact: This fluttery feeling and excitement often mix together right before a thrilling ride!

quests.instruction: Your neighbor's family is going on a big vacation and yours is not. How do you feel?
quests.question: Jealous
quests.hint: Hearing about someone else's exciting plans while yours stay the same can feel uncomfortable.
quests.explanation: Hearing about someone else's exciting plans, while yours stay the same, can give you a wanting feeling.
quests.funFact: Planning your own fun activity at home can help turn this feeling into excitement instead.

quests.instruction: You do not make the final round of the spelling bee. How do you feel?
quests.question: Disappointed
quests.hint: Studying hard for a competition and not moving forward can leave you feeling let down.
quests.explanation: Studying hard for a competition and not moving forward can leave you with a heavy, letdown feeling.
quests.funFact: Every round of a spelling bee still teaches you new words you will remember!

quests.instruction: Your stomach growls loudly during a quiet test. How do you feel?
quests.question: Embarrassed
quests.hint: A loud, unexpected sound from your own body in a silent room can make your cheeks warm up.
quests.explanation: A loud, unexpected sound in a silent room can make your cheeks feel warm and a little shy.
quests.funFact: A growling stomach is just a normal sign that it is almost time to eat — everyone's does it!

quests.instruction: A classmate lends you a pencil when yours breaks. How do you feel?
quests.question: Thankful
quests.hint: Being helped out of a small problem by someone kind can make your heart feel warm.
quests.explanation: Being helped out of a small problem by someone kind fills you with a warm, grateful feeling.
quests.funFact: Small acts of kindness, like sharing a pencil, can make a classroom feel friendlier for everyone!

quests.instruction: You are about to show your parents your report card. How do you feel?
quests.question: Nervous
quests.hint: Waiting to share important news can make your stomach feel fluttery.
quests.explanation: Waiting to share something important with your parents can give you a fluttery feeling.
quests.funFact: Talking about it calmly with a grown-up usually helps this fluttery feeling settle down.

quests.instruction: Your teammate gets to be team captain instead of you. How do you feel?
quests.question: Jealous
quests.hint: Missing out on a role you wanted while someone else gets it can feel uncomfortable.
quests.explanation: Missing out on a role you wanted can give you an uncomfortable, wanting feeling inside.
quests.funFact: Being a great teammate, even without the captain title, still helps the whole team succeed!

quests.instruction: Your favorite ride at the amusement park is closed for repairs. How do you feel?
quests.question: Disappointed
quests.hint: Really looking forward to something and finding out it is unavailable can leave you feeling let down.
quests.explanation: Really looking forward to something and finding it unavailable can leave you feeling let down.
quests.funFact: Rides get repaired to make sure they are extra safe and fun for your very next visit!

quests.instruction: You accidentally walk into the wrong classroom. How do you feel?
quests.question: Embarrassed
quests.hint: Realizing you are in the wrong place while everyone looks up can make your cheeks feel warm.
quests.explanation: Realizing you are in the wrong place while everyone looks up can make you feel warm and shy.
quests.funFact: A quick 'sorry, wrong room!' and a smile is all it takes to move past this moment.

quests.instruction: A stranger returns the wallet you accidentally dropped. How do you feel?
quests.question: Thankful
quests.hint: Getting back something important because a stranger was honest can fill your heart with warmth.
quests.explanation: Getting back something important because a stranger was honest fills you with a warm, grateful feeling.
quests.funFact: Honesty from strangers is one of the kindest surprises — it helps people trust each other more!

quests.instruction: You are waiting for the dentist to call your name. How do you feel?
quests.question: Nervous
quests.hint: Waiting for an appointment you are unsure about can make your leg bounce.
quests.explanation: Waiting for an appointment you feel unsure about can give you a fluttery feeling.
quests.funFact: Bringing a favorite small toy to hold in the waiting room can help this feeling feel smaller.

quests.instruction: Your classmate's project gets picked to be shown to the whole school. How do you feel?
quests.question: Jealous
quests.hint: Watching someone else's hard work get special attention can give you an uncomfortable feeling.
quests.explanation: Watching someone else's work get special attention can give you an uncomfortable, wanting feeling.
quests.funFact: Congratulating a classmate, even with this feeling, is a skill that gets easier with practice!

quests.instruction: The toy you saved up for is sold out when you finally get to the store. How do you feel?
quests.question: Disappointed
quests.hint: Saving up for something and just missing it can leave you with a heavy feeling.
quests.explanation: Saving up for something and just missing your chance can leave you with a heavy, letdown feeling.
quests.funFact: Asking a store worker about a restock date can turn this feeling into hope again!

quests.instruction: You accidentally call your teacher 'mom.' How do you feel?
quests.question: Embarrassed
quests.hint: Saying the wrong word by accident in front of the class can make your face feel warm.
quests.explanation: Saying the wrong word by accident with everyone listening can make your cheeks feel warm.
quests.funFact: This exact mix-up happens to so many students that most teachers just smile and move on!

quests.instruction: Your teacher stays a few minutes late to help you understand a hard problem. How do you feel?
quests.question: Thankful
quests.hint: Someone giving up their own time just to help you can make your heart feel warm.
quests.explanation: Someone giving up their own time to help you fills your heart with a warm, grateful feeling.
quests.funFact: Teachers often say helping students understand something new is their favorite part of the day!

quests.instruction: You are about to meet your new classmate's family for the first time. How do you feel?
quests.question: Nervous
quests.hint: Meeting new people you want to make a good impression on can feel fluttery.
quests.explanation: Meeting new people for the first time can give you a fluttery, unsure feeling.
quests.funFact: A simple smile and a hello usually help this fluttery feeling settle quickly!

quests.instruction: Your cousin gets a new puppy and you are still waiting for one. How do you feel?
quests.question: Jealous
quests.hint: Watching someone else get something you have wanted for a long time can feel uncomfortable.
quests.explanation: Watching someone else get something you have wanted for a while can give you a wanting feeling.
quests.funFact: Visiting and playing with a friend's or cousin's puppy is a fun way to enjoy it too!

quests.instruction: Your team loses the championship game after playing so well all season. How do you feel?
quests.question: Disappointed
quests.hint: Working hard all season and still coming up short can leave you feeling let down.
quests.explanation: Working hard all season and still coming up short can leave you with a heavy, letdown feeling.
quests.funFact: Coaches often say a great season is about more than just the final score!

quests.instruction: You realize you have been singing the wrong words to a song out loud. How do you feel?
quests.question: Embarrassed
quests.hint: Discovering you got the words wrong in front of others can make your cheeks feel warm.
quests.explanation: Discovering you got the words wrong in front of others can make you feel warm and a little shy.
quests.funFact: Getting song lyrics wrong is so common that it even has a name: a 'mondegreen'!

quests.instruction: Your older sister helps you study for your spelling test. How do you feel?
quests.question: Thankful
quests.hint: Having someone patiently help you get ready for something important can feel very warm.
quests.explanation: Having someone patiently help you prepare for something important fills you with a warm, grateful feeling.
quests.funFact: Studying with someone who cares about you can also make learning feel more fun!

quests.instruction: You are about to take the stage for your very first piano recital. How do you feel?
quests.question: Nervous
quests.hint: Waiting to perform something new in front of an audience can make your hands feel shaky.
quests.explanation: Waiting to perform in front of an audience for the first time can give you a shaky, fluttery feeling.
quests.funFact: Many musicians say this feeling fades quickly once they start playing their first note.

quests.instruction: Your friend has way more stickers in their collection than you do. How do you feel?
quests.question: Jealous
quests.hint: Comparing your collection to a friend's bigger one can give you a small, wanting feeling.
quests.explanation: Comparing your collection to someone else's bigger one can give you a small, wanting feeling.
quests.funFact: Trading stickers with a friend is a fun way collections can grow for everyone!

quests.instruction: The book series you love ends without the ending you were hoping for. How do you feel?
quests.question: Disappointed
quests.hint: A story not turning out the way you hoped can leave you with a heavy, letdown feeling.
quests.explanation: A story not turning out the way you hoped can leave you with a heavy, letdown feeling.
quests.funFact: Many readers write their own alternate endings when a story does not go the way they hoped!

quests.instruction: You wave at someone who was actually waving at a person behind you. How do you feel?
quests.question: Embarrassed
quests.hint: Realizing you misread a small moment in front of others can make your face feel warm.
quests.explanation: Realizing you misread a small moment can make your cheeks feel warm and a little shy.
quests.funFact: This kind of little mix-up happens to almost everyone at some point — it is very common!

quests.instruction: Your friend saves you a seat on the bus every morning. How do you feel?
quests.question: Thankful
quests.hint: Knowing someone always thinks of you can fill your heart with warmth.
quests.explanation: Knowing a friend always thinks of you fills your heart with a warm, grateful feeling.
quests.funFact: Small daily kindnesses like saved seats often build the strongest friendships!

quests.instruction: You are getting ready for your very first day of swim lessons. How do you feel?
quests.question: Nervous
quests.hint: Trying something brand new in front of a new teacher can make your stomach flutter.
quests.explanation: Trying something brand new with a new teacher watching can give you a fluttery feeling.
quests.funFact: Swim teachers work with beginners every single day — they are used to helping this feeling fade!
